dataset.name: WTC 1 V8L multistory cold core frame
dataset.scope: Floors 94-99; explicit vertical column segments and floor-by-floor beam transfer under the NIST Case B post-impact core load at 20 C
dataset.warning: The model is a scalar vertical-displacement spring network, not a shell/beam finite-element reproduction. The orthogonal topology and WF assignments are bounded reconstructions because Drawing Books 5 and 6 and the adjusted global-model slab modulus are unavailable.

official_facts.label: RESULTAT_MODELE_OFFICIEL
official_facts.fact: Figure 2-17 maps the WTC 1 Case B severed or heavily damaged core-column segments between Floors 91 and 97.

official_facts.label: RESULTAT_MODELE_OFFICIEL_LIMITE
official_facts.fact: The isolated WTC 1 core model extended from Floor 89 to Floor 106 and included columns, core beams and slabs. Case B structural-damage runs did not converge even with lateral restraints. The isolated model did not capture transfer between core and exterior walls through floors or the hat truss.

official_facts.label: RESULTAT_MODELE_OFFICIEL
official_facts.fact: The global model used equivalent vertical springs at its truncated base. Individually modeled core beams were those with moment connections; non-moment beam axial stiffness was combined with the in-plane slab stiffness. NIST states that the composite floor representation could redistribute load locally among neighboring columns.

official_facts.label: RESULTAT_MODELE_OFFICIEL
official_facts.fact: After impact, loads from severed columns were redistributed mostly to neighboring columns. At Floor 98 the core carried about one percent more gravity load; Column 705 buckled and Columns 605 and 804 showed minor buckling.

nist_moment_only.source: NIST NCSTAR 1-6D Figure 4-2 / prior V8H transcription
nist_moment_only.note: Only individually modeled moment-connected core beams; 500 and 1000 series are not connected in this subnetwork.

orthogonal_floor96_reconstruction.source: NIST NCSTAR 1-6C Figure 5-59(a) registered to Figure 2-2
orthogonal_floor96_reconstruction.construction: Consecutive columns within each numbered row plus same-terminal-digit links between adjacent rows.
orthogonal_floor96_reconstruction.note: No nearest-four diagonals are used. The graph is an envelope for beams plus omitted composite-floor transfer, not an as-built schedule.

beam_damage_definition.source_status: Figure-constrained Case Ai Floor 96 transcription from V8K
beam_damage_definition.warning: The refined Case B core-beam damage map by floor is unavailable. Repeating the Floor 96 pattern over Floors 94-98 is a conservative sensitivity, not an official damage assignment.

mechanical_laws.columns: Elastic axial EA/L springs capped by the V8B room-temperature nominal compressive capacity for each historic WF proxy. Case B severed/heavy segments are removed before loading.
mechanical_laws.beams: V8H bilinear vertical-transfer law: k=12EI/L^3, Vy=connection_factor*2Mp/L, one floor plane, 1 percent post-yield tangent, fracture at 0.02 rad relative rotation.
mechanical_laws.column_failure: A column spring is removed if compressive force exceeds its V8B nominal room-temperature capacity.
omitted: explicit shell slab bending and cracking
published adjusted slab modulus because its numeric value is unavailable
column and joint rotational degrees of freedom

gate.required_condition: The Case B cold load must reach the Floor 93 support without a disconnected loaded component or capacity-triggered cascade in at least one physically sourced topology; a reconstructed upper envelope alone cannot validate the as-built path.
gate.thermal_authorization_rule: Thermal continuation remains blocked if only the reconstructed orthogonal envelope passes or if every core-only case fails.
